newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan selects new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan selects new chief executive.

text.p: Struggling fashion design company Donna Karan Intl. said Monday it selected an executive from Polo Ralph Lauren Corp. to take over as the company's chief executive officer.

The new chief executive, John Idol, a group president and divisional chief operating officer responsible for the Ralph Lauren Clothing Company, will take the new position on Aug. 11, Donna Karan said.
He replaces company founder Donna Karan, who will give up the chief executive position but remain chairman and chief designer.
In his new position, Idol will be responsible for "strategic leadership," Karan said.

"A global company of this size and complexity needs one person who can concentrate on the business and lead its management. It is important, both for me and for the company, that I concentrate on my greatest strengths -- the company's vision, the marketing and creative aspects of the business and its growth initiatives," Karan said in a statement announcing Idol's appointment.
Idol 38, has been at Polo Ralph Lauren for 13 years and most recently was in charge of overseeing select wholesale and licensed businesses that accounted for about $1.7 billion in annual revenues.

Donna Karan has been struggling since it went public a year ago. In May it announced a restructuring that included a 4 percent cut in its workforce, a hiring freeze and steps to reduce its expenses by $4.8 million.

The company's stock has fallen from its initial public offering of $24 a share to a low of $8.875 earlier this year. The stock was at $11.625, up $1.19 in early consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
